title: introduce-cost-decision-compiler-and-tenant-presets-cli
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: teams often iterate on batching, cache and quantization defaults manually per-tenant. This PR adds a deterministic compiler that converts high-level tenant cost policies into a compact runtime preset (tenant-profile) and a developer-facing CLI to author, validate, and preview the expected unit-economics impact. The goal is to reduce manual tuning, enable safe automated rollouts, and give platform engineers a reproducible artifact to load at startup. Summary of changes: 1) cost/decision-compiler: new package that compiles policy rules (batch size targets, cache TTLs, quant profile hints, tolerance windows) into a normalized tenant-profile.json; compiler supports a dry-run mode that simulates token-cost impact using sampled request traces and a small synthetic traffic generator; 2) cli/redwood-costctl: new subcommand `compile` with `--preview` and `--simulate N` options plus `--output` to emit profiles; 3) runtime/loader: lightweight tenant-profile loader at boot with safe validation and fallback-to-default behavior; 4) telemetry: added unit_econ.preview.* tags and compile.duration_ms histograms to help observe compiler impact; 5) docs: new guide in docs/operational/cost-compiler.md and CLI reference; 6) tests: integration test that runs compile+simulate against a small trace and asserts cost deltas within acceptable bounds. Backwards compatibility: tenant-profile loader falls back to legacy defaults when profile is syntactically invalid or version mismatch. Rollout plan: start with opt-in tenant alpha, gather metrics for 2 weeks, enable auto-apply for tenants with low variance. Related work: builds on ENG-4211 (batching-safety-gates) and PM-1010 (tenant-cost-surface).
commit_summary:
commit 1: add cost/decision-compiler core algorithm and schema
commit 2: add CLI subcommand and argument parsing with preview/simulate flags
commit 3: runtime loader and validation + fallback behavior
commit 4: telemetry and metrics hooks for compile/preview
commit 5: docs and examples + unit/integration tests
commit 6: fix: resilience on missing sample traces and improve error messages

review_thread: Diego Alvarez: Please add a failure-mode test for when the sample traces are missing. Compiler currently returns 500 rather than a validation error.
Maya Chen: Added integration test to assert compile returns structured error and loader falls back. See tests/integration/compile_simulate_test.go

Maya Chen: Done — added telemetry labels unit_econ.preview.tenant_id and policy_hash in telemetry/metrics.go
Luca Romano: Suggest tightening the default quantization tolerance from 0.15 -> 0.10 for canary to reduce quality regressions. Consider parameterizing per-deployment.

merge_summary: Merged by Priya Nambiar (squash) on 2025-03-04. Squash commit message: 'introduce cost decision compiler + costctl compile CLI; runtime loader and docs'
release_notes: Added: 'redwood-costctl compile' CLI to produce tenant-profile artifacts; compiler that converts high-level cost policies into runtime-ready presets; preview/simulate mode to estimate unit-economic impact. Runtime: tenant-profile loader with safe validation and fallback. Telemetry: unit_econ.preview.* metrics. Docs: operational guide for compiler and rollout recommendations.
notes_for_ops: Enable beta by setting ENV ENABLE_TENANT_COMPILER=true and configure sample traces path SAMPLE_TRACE_PATH; initial rollout should use --simulate 1000 and run under staging for 7–14 days. CLI output includes a JSON artifact suitable for S3 storage and later boot-time consumption.
manual_backports: cherry-pick to release/2025-03 required for customers on locked deployment; apply only the runtime loader and schema compatibility checks (cost/decision-compiler/schema.go and runtime/tenant_loader.go)
qa_checklist: validate fallback by corrupting profile version and ensure loader falls back
verify unit_econ.preview.* metrics appear in staging dashboards
safety_considerations: Compiler output is non-authoritative until operator applies it; runtime always validates version and falls back to tenant defaults. Compiler simulation uses sampled traces and may under/overestimate tail latency for small sample sizes — docs recommend >=5000 samples for high-volume tenants.
